# A unit spec whose import chain reaches manager/Window at top level loads only after another spec ran in its worker: the setup installs Neo.currentWorker after the hoisted imports

## Problem

`test/playwright/setup.mjs` installs the `Neo.currentWorker` mock inside `setup()`, which a spec calls in its module body — after every static import has been evaluated, because ES imports are hoisted. `src/manager/Window.mjs` creates its singleton at import time and its `construct` calls `Neo.currentWorker.on(...)`. A spec whose static import chain reaches the window manager therefore throws at load, and Playwright reports the file as having no tests.

The chain exists on `dev` since 2026-08-30: `examples/dashboard/crossWindow/DemoBWorkspace.mjs` imports `src/ai/client/InteractionService.mjs` (since 08-23), which gained `import WindowManager from '../../manager/Window.mjs'` with the atomic drag transactions (#17862). `test/playwright/unit/examples/dashboard/crossWindow/DemoBWorkspace.spec.mjs` has not been runnable alone since.

CI does not see it because Playwright reuses a worker's Node process across spec files and `globalThis.Neo` survives that reuse: when another spec ran first in the same worker, its `setup()` already installed the mock, and the example spec loads and passes. With four CI workers and sixty-odd files that is nearly always the case. Alone, or first in its worker, it is dead. Measured: `npx playwright test -c playwright.config.unit.mjs unit/examples/dashboard/crossWindow/DemoBWorkspace.spec.mjs` → `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'on')` at `src/manager/Window.mjs:40`, "No tests found", exit 1; the same file after `unit/dashboard/DockActionTooltips.spec.mjs` with `--workers=1` → loads, 64 tests run. Same result with CI's invocation (`NEO_TEST_SKIP_CI=true npm run test-unit -- <file>`).

This class has been seen before from the other side: a local namespace collision killing every service-importing unit spec while CI stayed unaffected, and the theme-deferral gate reading a stale worker binding across worker reuse. The shared cause is state that lives on `globalThis.Neo` across files in one worker.

## Evidence

- `test/playwright/setup.mjs`: top level sets `globalThis.Neo ??= {}`, `Neo.config` and `DOMRect`; `Neo.currentWorker ??= {...}` sits inside `setup()`.
- `src/manager/Window.mjs:40` (`construct`) and `:230` (singleton at import).
- `src/ai/client/InteractionService.mjs:2` — the static import; `examples/dashboard/crossWindow/DemoBWorkspace.mjs:17`.
- Only `test/playwright/unit/data/PipelineRemoteExecution.spec.mjs` assigns its own `Neo.currentWorker`, by plain assignment with restore — unaffected by an earlier default.

## Proposed change

Move the `Neo.currentWorker ??= {...}` block to the module top level of `setup.mjs`, next to `globalThis.Neo ??= {}`: `setup.mjs` is every spec's first import, so its top level runs before any engine module evaluates. `??=` keeps a spec's own later assignment authoritative and keeps `setup()`'s behaviour for every other spec identical. No change to the window manager: constructing its singleton at import is its production shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `DemoBWorkspace.spec.mjs` runs alone (`npx playwright test -c playwright.config.unit.mjs <file>`) and finds and passes its tests; it also passes first in a `--workers=1` pair.
- [ ] The full unit suite stays green; `PipelineRemoteExecution.spec.mjs` keeps its own worker seam.
- [ ] The moved block's comment states why it lives at top level (hoisted imports evaluate before `setup()`).

## Non-goals

- Making the window manager tolerate a missing worker at import.
- The worker-reuse class in general (a lint that spots `globalThis.Neo` state leaking across files) — a separate leaf if wanted.

Found while adding a unit arm to that spec for #18088; the arm is blocked on this. Sweep 13:50Z before filing: live latest-20 open (no match), A2A last-8 (no claim), Knowledge Base (#15364 and #16503 are the same class from other causes, neither this).
